rejectedSkills.reason: Strong candidate on its own merits (relevance 2, quality 3, conformance 2 — a clean, self-contained, spec-minimal SKILL.md pushing for a committed, distinctive aesthetic direction with concrete typography/color/motion/composition rules), but its upstream frontmatter name 'frontend-design' is an exact id collision with BOTH the registry's already-catalogued 'frontend-design' entry AND an already-completed vendor manifest for that same id produced earlier in this research campaign (research/manifests/frontend-design.json, sourced from anthropics/skills, rubric 3/3/2/2=10, recommended:true). Writing a second manifest under the same id would silently overwrite that decided, higher-scoring candidate. Not vendored to avoid the collision; the overlap is recorded for curator awareness in case they prefer this opendesign version, or want to fold ideas from both (this one's oklch chroma-restriction rule and named 'aesthetic direction' taxonomy — brutalist/maximalist/editorial/retro-futuristic/organic/industrial/anti-design/swiss-modernist/zine-punk — are not present in the anthropics version).

Good instructions in isolation (explicit required output paths, a numbered process from asset exploration through UI-kit build, hard rules against inventing components or hand-drawing SVGs), but held back by two things: (1) it is tightly coupled to opendesign's own tooling — every generated system MUST write to exact non-negotiable paths under ./opendesign/design-systems/<name>/ so opendesign's own auto-discovery logic can find it, and step 8 explicitly says 'Use the deck skill's conventions', a soft dependency on the make-a-deck sibling that only partially transfers once vendored standalone; (2) it substantially overlaps ground already covered by three already-catalogued/vendored registry ids (design-system, design-tokens, design-system-governance, plus the already-vendored research/manifests/design-system.json from anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins). Excluded under the repo's 4-skill vendoring cap in favor of handoff-to-claude-code, which is more portable (conformance 2 vs 1) and less redundant with what is already vendored.

Covers a genuinely novel niche (an in-design 'Tweaks' panel with an ordered activate/deactivate postMessage handshake and multiple persistence strategies) that nothing else in the registry or this campaign's manifests touches, but it assumes a specific host architecture — a parent iframe/window that posts 'activate'/'deactivate' messages and expects an availability announcement back — which is opendesign-viewer-specific host coupling rather than a self-sufficient, portable instruction set. It also scored lowest of the repo's design-relevant skills and the brief caps vendoring at 4 for this repo.

The repo's main orchestrator skill (routes to the other 9 specialist skills, defines the base designer role and workflow). Fails the strict self-containment rule: its workflow explicitly dispatches subagents 'using the setup-opendesign skill' and 'using the run-opendesign skill' by name — both of which are rejected below (setup-opendesign for a live download-and-write security concern, run-opendesign for zero design relevance) and are therefore not being vendored as siblings. Bundling them back in to satisfy self-containment would mean vendoring exactly the two skills already rejected on their own merits, which the brief does not intend. Named external dependency: the setup-opendesign and run-opendesign sibling skills (for subagent dispatch) and a live fetch of skills/opendesign/viewer.html from raw.githubusercontent.com (for first-run setup) — none of which resolve inside a standalone 'opendesign' skill directory. not-vendored-keeper in substance (license and content quality are fine); grouped here under the repo's reject file per the required output shape.

Pure local dev-server/runtime tooling (detect platform, check port 8289, start a python/node static file server, print a localhost link). No design activity content whatsoever — it is infrastructure for opendesign's own preview workflow, not something a product-design agent skill registry catalogs. Automatic reject on relevance alone.

Zero design content — pure first-run installer (create folders, write an empty manifest.json). It also fails the rubric's automatic-disqualifier bar on its own terms: step 1 instructs the agent to fetch skills/opendesign/viewer.html live from raw.githubusercontent.com on every fresh-project run and write the response body directly into the user's project as ./opendesign/index.html, with no pinning, hash check, or review step — content that can change upstream at any time and is written into the user's project unreviewed. That is a download-and-write pattern the rubric's automatic disqualifiers flag as unreviewable/supply-chain risk, on top of already being irrelevant to design work.
